# Reusable Blender studio (setup only)

**State:** Tooling and empty production interfaces only. **No scenes, characters, models, animations, rendered images, or finished media are generated by this setup.**

- **Blender 4.5.16 LTS**, installed from the Blender Foundation release and SHA-256 checked against its official checksum manifest.
- Headless Python/Blender environment probe and production-contract validation. Nothing is installed on the user's computer.
- Explicit local-only asset registry with per-asset rights, source link and SHA-256. It starts EMPTY.
- Generic shot, rig, camera, render-quality, importer and audio-integration interfaces for when we actually make a film.
- Automatic [Blender environment setup](../.github/workflows/blender-environment.yml) only validates software and contracts. Manual [Blender rendering](../.github/workflows/blender-render.yml) requires an explicit existing authorized .blend source and user dispatch.
- Existing HyperFrames/Kokoro audio pipeline and previous films are untouched.

## Remote workflow

1. Check GitHub > Actions > Blender environment setup. It verifies installation, Blender APIs and metadata without creating film frames.
2. To add assets later, review license on the original publisher's page, store the file in a private working directory, measure SHA-256 and add an approved entry to [assets/registry.json](assets/registry.json). The importer refuses mismatches and unapproved entries.
3. For future film production, prepare a project manifest following [production schema](schemas/production.schema.json), shot manifests and actual .blend files. See [production workflow](PRODUCTION.md).
4. Render manually after reviewing the scene. Large media, third-party files and private tokens must not be committed to this public repository.

## Setup files

- config/toolchain.json: pinned Blender, profiles and output policy
- config/asset-sources.json: catalog of providers to inspect; does not download
- assets/registry.json: approved provenance ledger (initially empty)
- schemas/: machine-readable production and shot contracts
- studio/: Blender-independent manifest validation and bpy-based production helpers
- scripts/: verified cloud installer, no-media environment probe, explicit future import and render entry points
- tests/: no-scene Python unit tests

**VRM v4.10.5/MToon is installed and verified** on the GitHub runner from a SHA-256-pinned release. No models were imported. **Rigify is deferred** because the public Blender Extensions listing has availability warnings; the existing VRM humanoid support and studio IK helpers do not require it.

Official docs: https://www.blender.org/download/LTS/ , https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/4.5/advanced/command_line/arguments.html , https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/4.5/advanced/command_line/extension_arguments.html .

## Verified extension integration

- [Pinned VRM/MToon installer](scripts/install_vrm_extension.sh) and [non-rendering API probe](scripts/vrm_doctor.py): both passed on GitHub Actions.
- [Manual future asset conversion](scripts/import_registered_asset.py): can import a legally approved model and save a new editable blend, but is never run by setup.
- [Reusable Blender agent skill](skills/studio/SKILL.md): cinematography, body mechanics, asset rights, audio integration and safety checklist.
- Approved assets remain at **zero**. The setup generated **zero** frames or scenes.
